keyTerms.definition: The exam questions that count toward the score. Domain 5 has about 7 of 65.
Programmatic scores computed by code against ground truth labels.
The Bedrock API that starts an evaluation job.

recall.question: How many scored Domain 5 questions are on the exam?
recall.answer: About 7 of the 65 scored questions.

recall.question: Which evaluation features were fact-checked against live AWS docs on 2026-09-28?
recall.answer: Automatic metrics, LLM-as-a-judge metric names, human workflows, BYO datasets, and CreateEvaluationJob.

keyTerms.definition: The proof half of the domain. It measures whether the GenAI application works.
The fix half of the domain. It repairs the application when it does not work.
A second model that grades outputs, giving human-like quality at scale.
Evaluations that check retrieval quality and faithfulness in RAG pipelines.

recall.question: What one question does Domain 5 ask in many forms?
recall.answer: How do you prove a GenAI application works, and how do you fix it when it does not work.

recall.question: Name two proof-half tools and what each is for.
recall.answer: Automatic metrics do objective checks. LLM-as-a-judge gives human-like quality at scale.

sections.title: 1. Why testing generative AI is different

keyTerms.definition: The unit of measurement. It has a prompt dataset, a run, and a scoring step.
The known-correct answer attached to a prompt for scoring.
Same input always gives the same output. True of traditional tests, not model calls.
The generation setting that controls randomness. It shapes wording, never correctness.
A test style that fails open-ended outputs. Never use it there.

recall.question: What are the three parts of an eval?
recall.answer: A dataset of prompts, a run that feeds each prompt to the model, and a scoring step that judges each output.

recall.question: A checkout total must equal 42.50 character for character. Why does this test style not fit GenAI?
recall.answer: It is a deterministic assertion: one input, one correct output, pass or fail. GenAI has many valid outputs and nondeterministic wording.

recall.question: What does temperature control, and what does it never do?
recall.answer: It controls randomness and shapes wording. It never shapes correctness and is never a cost control.

sections.title: What AWS actually tests (the evaluation matrix)

keyTerms.definition: The table mapping each method to what it measures. It is the main part of Task 5.1.
Programmatic evaluation of accuracy, stability, and toxicity against ground truth labels.
The exam task that the evaluation matrix covers.

recall.question: What does the evaluation matrix map?
recall.answer: Each evaluation method to what it measures and when AWS wants it.

recall.question: How do you read the three-family diagram?
recall.answer: The left column names quality, safety, and groundedness with their metrics. The right box names automatic metrics, LLM-as-judge, and human review. Arrows link each family to all three methods.

keyTerms.definition: A fixed set of trusted prompts that you rerun after every change.
A release to a small part of traffic before full rollout.
The exam question style. Every question hides a team situation, not a bare definition.

recall.question: A team must compare two models for summarization quality and brand voice. Which two methods?
recall.answer: LLM-as-a-judge for scale and human evaluation for brand voice.

recall.question: What is the domain-wide trap in every troubleshooting question?
recall.answer: One wrong answer debugs GenAI like a traditional app. Temperature does not fix bad retrieval. Bigger models do not fix broken chunking. Provisioned Throughput does not fix output randomness.

keyTerms.definition: Bedrock's cheapest and fastest mode. Code computes metrics with no humans or judge.
The correct answer you already know, attached to each prompt in the dataset.
A pipeline step that stops a deployment if quality scores drop.
The Bedrock console name for the stability metric.
JSON Lines, one record per line. The S3 format for prompt datasets.
A built-in metric that checks outputs for toxic content.

recall.question: What four items does an evaluation job need?
recall.answer: The model to evaluate, the prompt dataset in S3 as JSONL, an output S3 location, and the evaluation configuration naming the metrics.

recall.question: A 1,000-prompt ticket classifier scores 0.93 accuracy. What does that number mean, and what did it cost?
recall.answer: 930 of 1,000 outputs matched the ground truth label exactly. It cost a few dollars at most and finished in minutes.

recall.question: When must you NOT use automatic evaluation?
recall.answer: For subjective quality like brand voice, style, or helpfulness. Programmatic scorers compare labels and cannot judge tone.

keyTerms.definition: The built-in metric for correct-answer rate against labeled data.
The metric to add when outputs contain toxic phrases.
Prompts with known-correct answers. The signal for automatic evaluation.

recall.question: EASY: 3,000 labeled customer questions, cheap repeatable benchmark to pick between two small models. Correct approach?
recall.answer: Run a Bedrock automatic evaluation job with the accuracy metric on the labeled dataset.

recall.question: MEDIUM: 0.97 accuracy but toxic phrases in apologies, and the job used only accuracy. What must the team do?
recall.answer: Add the toxicity metric to the evaluation configuration and run the job again.

recall.question: HARD: two true statements about automatic evaluation as a regression gate?
recall.answer: It needs ground truth labels to compute metrics like accuracy, and it supports built-in metrics including accuracy, stability, and toxicity.

keyTerms.definition: Bring-your-own. You supply the evaluation prompts as JSONL in S3.
Bring-your-own-inference. You supply prompts and your own responses. It trains nothing.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall. It tells the truth on imbalanced data.
Of the items labeled X, how many are truly X.
How many X items the system labeled X.
The summarization metric measuring overlap between generated and reference summaries.

recall.question: The worked ticket-classifier example: 1,000 tickets, 950 correct, but urgent-class F1 is 0.44. What is the exam lesson?
recall.answer: Accuracy lies on imbalanced data. F1 tells the truth.

recall.question: A fraud classifier sees 1 percent fraud. Which metric, and why not accuracy?
recall.answer: F1 or precision and recall. Accuracy is dominated by the majority class.

recall.question: What does BYOI let you evaluate, and what does it not do?
recall.answer: Any system: a model outside Bedrock, a full RAG pipeline, an agent with tools, or replayed production responses. It trains nothing.

keyTerms.definition: The team's own labeled tickets, brought for evaluation.
The rare class where recall matters more than accuracy.
What BYOI submits for evaluation.

recall.question: EASY: 2,000 labeled tickets routed into 12 categories. Correct setup?
recall.answer: Bring the labeled tickets as a BYO dataset and run automatic evaluation with accuracy and F1.

recall.question: MEDIUM: 0.99 accuracy on old data but most fraud still passes, and only 0.5 percent of transactions are fraud. Best metric change?
recall.answer: Change to F1 score with emphasis on recall for the fraud class.

keyTerms.definition: A foundation model scores another model's outputs against a rubric you define.
The anti-hallucination metric. The source supports every claim.
Judges favor the first answer. Bedrock fights it by randomizing order.
Judges favor longer answers.
The metric for covering all requests in the prompt.
The metric for correctly declining what the model should decline.

recall.question: What are the four flow stages of a judge evaluation?
recall.answer: Candidate generation, judge prompt assembly, judgment, and aggregation.

recall.question: The RAG summarizer example: 500 prompts, small candidate, flagship judge. What did the numbers show?
recall.answer: Total cost about $10.50 in under one hour. Correctness 4.2 of 5, faithfulness 3.6 of 5, style 4.5 of 5. The faithfulness gap pointed to retrieval grounding, not tone.

recall.question: What are the two traps when using judge models?
recall.answer: Do not treat judge scores as true data without human spot-check calibration, and do not use the same small model as both candidate and judge.

keyTerms.definition: The judge metrics for the 4,000-response RAG check.
A small model grading outputs. It cannot grade reliably and may share blind spots.
Compare judge scores with human labels on a sample before trusting full runs.

recall.question: EASY: 4,000 responses, faithfulness and correct refusal, no true labels. Best method?
recall.answer: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation with faithfulness and refusal metrics.

recall.question: MEDIUM: same small model as candidate and judge, scores too high versus human spot-check. Most probable cause?
recall.answer: A weak judge model cannot reliably grade outputs and may share the candidate's blind spots.

keyTerms.definition: How often reviewers agree. It shows whether the instructions are clear.
The reviewers: your employees or an AWS-managed team.
The AWS-managed crowd reviewers for human evaluation.
The budget unit: responses times reviewers per response times minutes per rating, over 60.
Concrete score meanings, like 5 equals a full example, written into rating instructions.

recall.question: How do you budget a human evaluation?
recall.answer: Reviewer-hours equals responses times reviewers per response times minutes per rating, divided by 60. The example: 300 times 3 times 2 minutes equals 30 reviewer-hours.

recall.question: Agreement is 0.82 on accuracy but 0.54 on warmth. What does that tell you?
recall.answer: The warmth instructions are vague. Rewrite the anchors with concrete examples and re-run.

recall.question: State the standard pattern for the three methods.
recall.answer: Automatic metrics for the main part, LLM-as-a-judge for subjective scale, human evaluation for samples, calibration, and final approval.

keyTerms.definition: The subjective quality the AWS-managed team reviews.
The reviewers to use when no employees are available.
Human evaluation's role for subjective qualities on high-risk responses.

recall.question: EASY: marketing text, brand voice matters most, no employees can review. Best setup?
recall.answer: LLM-as-a-judge for general comparison plus human evaluation with an AWS-managed review team for brand voice.

recall.question: MEDIUM: agreement 0.85 for correctness, 0.51 for helpfulness. Best next step?
recall.answer: Rewrite the helpfulness rating instructions with clear examples, then run again on a sample.

sections.title: 6. RAG evaluation: retrieval quality, faithfulness, relevance

keyTerms.definition: Scoring retrieval and generation separately instead of only the final answer.
How many chunks with the answer appear in the top k retrieved chunks.
The metric checking whether the answer addresses the question.
Every factual claim in the answer must come from the retrieved context.
Whether the retrieved chunks are on topic for the question.

recall.question: How do you read the retrieval and faithfulness score pair?
recall.answer: Low retrieval plus low faithfulness means fix retrieval: chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, or reranking. High retrieval plus low faithfulness means fix generation: grounding instructions or contextual grounding checks.

recall.question: The support RAG example: recall at 5 of 0.70, faithfulness 0.62. What fixed it?
recall.answer: Changing chunking from fixed-size to hierarchical and adding a reranker. Recall at 5 rose to 0.88 and faithfulness to 0.81, with no generator or prompt change.

recall.question: What is the most common Domain 5 trap?
recall.answer: Fixing bad retrieval by changing the generation model. If retrieved chunks are not relevant, no model can make a correct answer.

keyTerms.definition: What to evaluate when answers cite facts not in the documents.
The chunks with answers that recall at k compares against.

recall.question: EASY: fluent answers cite policy details not in retrieved documents, but retrieval relevance is high. Evaluate and fix what first?
recall.answer: Evaluate generation faithfulness and strengthen grounding of answers to retrieved context.

recall.question: MEDIUM: after a chunking change, recall at 5 drops from 0.90 to 0.71 while faithfulness stays 0.85. Correct interpretation?
recall.answer: The new chunking made retrieval bad. The generator uses the information it gets. Change or adjust chunking.

sections.title: 7. Eval loops and iteration: regression, canary, golden datasets

keyTerms.definition: A continuous process that re-runs the quality suite on every change.
Re-running a fixed suite and comparing results to the last good baseline.
A curated, versioned set of prompts with trusted expected outputs.
Releasing the change to a small part of traffic first and watching real metrics.
Slow quality decay when user behavior or source documents change with no prompt edits.

recall.question: What are the five stages of the loop?
recall.answer: Curate the golden dataset, baseline, change and compare, canary, promote or roll back.

recall.question: The support-assistant example: what failed the gate and why?
recall.answer: Faithfulness dropped from 0.88 to 0.79 and refusal correctness from 0.97 to 0.91, past the 0.03 threshold, because the shortened prompt removed the grounding instruction.

recall.question: The suite passes but users report new failure modes. What is the gap?
recall.answer: The golden dataset lacks those failure modes. Add prompts from every production incident to the dataset.

keyTerms.definition: Running a versioned golden-dataset suite on every prompt change and gating deployment.
What the golden-dataset suite compares metrics against.

recall.question: EASY: weekly system-prompt edits need an automated check before users see problems. What should they implement?
recall.answer: Regression testing: run a versioned golden-dataset evaluation suite on every prompt change and gate deployment on the scores.

recall.question: MEDIUM: the suite passes every time but users report multi-turn failures. Most probable gap?
recall.answer: The golden dataset has no multi-turn prompts, so the loop cannot see this failure mode.

keyTerms.definition: Online experimentation that serves versions to different live-traffic parts and compares results.
Parallel prompt choices for comparison, made in Bedrock Prompt Management.
Fixed snapshots for release and rollback. Sequential, not parallel.
Keeping one session on one variant so the comparison stays valid.
What the winner needs before it is declared.

recall.question: The two-prompt example: variant A has 78 percent resolution at $0.0050, variant B 76 percent at $0.0028. Who wins and why?
recall.answer: Variant B. The 2-point resolution gap is not significant at this sample size, but cost differs 44 percent, saving about $2.20 per 1,000 conversations with no measurable quality loss.

recall.question: What breaks an A/B test without sticky routing?
recall.answer: One user's session mixes variants, so answers change style mid-conversation and the comparison is invalid.

recall.question: Versions versus variants: what is the difference?
recall.answer: Versions are fixed snapshots for release and rollback. Variants are parallel choices for comparison.

keyTerms.definition: How to serve two prompts to live traffic with minimal code changes.
Traffic routing where users experience one variant all the time.

recall.question: EASY: two system prompts, similar offline scores, real traffic must decide, and marketing needs no-deploy wording changes. Best method?
recall.answer: Use Bedrock Prompt Management variants for the two prompts, split live traffic, and compare resolution, cost, and safety metrics.

recall.question: MEDIUM: answers change style mid-conversation during an A/B test. Most probable cause?
recall.answer: The router is not sticky, so one session changes between variants.

keyTerms.definition: The specific error pattern that points to the failing layer.
Bedrock errors when requests exceed allocated capacity.
The identifier the code must invoke to actually use purchased capacity.
The step to run after changing an agent's action groups.
What to check when knowledge base answers go stale.
The agent setting that surfaces failures in the trace.

recall.question: A team buys Provisioned Throughput but still gets throttled, and the code calls invoke_model with the base model ID. What is the fix?
recall.answer: Route invocations to the provisioned model ARN. Capacity was not the problem. Routing was.

recall.question: Knowledge base answers are stale after document updates. What is the fix, and what is the distractor?
recall.answer: Check the sync job. Switching the generation model is the distractor.

recall.question: What is the debug order for any GenAI incident?
recall.answer: Read the error, not the symptom. Throttling exceptions name the quota, guardrail blocks name the policy, agent failures appear with enableTrace, and KB sync status is in the console.

keyTerms.definition: What must run after adding an action group to a Bedrock agent.
What the code invokes instead of the provisioned ARN.
What must be rebuilt after switching embedding models.

recall.question: EASY: a new action group is added, the agent never calls the tool, and Lambda works directly. Most probable cause?
recall.answer: The prepare-agent step was not run after the configuration change. The agent still uses the old prepared version.

recall.question: HARD: the embedding model is switched, ingestion fails, and search collapses. Two correct statements?
recall.answer: Rebuild the vector index because the new model makes different-dimension vectors, and re-embed the corpus because old vectors cannot be reused.

sections.title: 10. Debugging with CloudWatch Logs and CloudTrail

keyTerms.definition: The metrics and logs service. It tells you what the application did.
The audit service. It tells you who called what, when, and from where.
Recording full Bedrock requests and responses to S3 or CloudWatch Logs.
CloudWatch alarms that catch token bursts or cost spikes.
The query tool for prompts, guardrail blocks, and error groups.

recall.question: How do the two services divide the debug loop?
recall.answer: CloudWatch shows the anomaly, Logs Insights shows the content, CloudTrail shows the actor.

recall.question: The token bill triples overnight with no traffic increase. What is the debug path?
recall.answer: OutputTokenCount shows the spike started at 02:00. Logs Insights shows one session looping 40,000-token responses. The agent trace shows a tool error retried forever. CloudTrail rules out a config change. The fix is a Step Functions stopping condition that caps iterations.

recall.question: Which service answers which IAM role invoked which model at 3 AM?
recall.answer: CloudTrail. It records every API call with the caller, time, source, and parameters.

keyTerms.definition: What CloudTrail is queried for to find who changed a guardrail policy.
What CloudWatch anomaly detection watches for spend alerts.

recall.question: EASY: which IAM principal changed a guardrail policy last Tuesday?
recall.answer: AWS CloudTrail, by querying the API call history for the guardrail update.

recall.question: MEDIUM: near-real-time token-spend alerts plus the prompts behind them. Correct combination?
recall.answer: CloudWatch anomaly detection on token-count metrics with an alarm, plus Bedrock model invocation logging queried in Logs Insights.

keyTerms.definition: The property that every fact in the response uses source content.
A claim with no source support: invented facts, wrong numbers, or answers from missing context.
The Bedrock Guardrails policy that scores grounding automatically.
The per-response score compared against the threshold you set.
The RAG evaluation metric measuring the same groundedness property offline.

recall.question: The product-support example: threshold 0.75, 300-question golden set, 40 traps. What happened?
recall.answer: The check blocked 37 of 40 traps, a 0.925 recall, but falsely blocked 8 correct answers. At 0.70, traps caught fell to 35 and false blocks to 3. The business accepted 35 of 40.

recall.question: Why does a grounding check not replace RAG evaluation?
recall.answer: The check enforces at runtime. The evaluation measures across the dataset. You need both.

recall.question: Verify the answer has support from the retrieved documents, versus verify the answer obeys the formal refund policy written as logic. Which control is which?
recall.answer: The first is contextual grounding. The second is Automated Reasoning.

keyTerms.definition: The Guardrails control for runtime hallucination enforcement.
The control that verifies answers obey formal policy rules written as logic.

recall.question: EASY: a RAG assistant invents product details, and the team needs runtime enforcement of source support. What should they use?
recall.answer: Bedrock Guardrails contextual grounding checks with a configured threshold.

recall.question: MEDIUM: answers must use the help articles, and refund decisions must follow logical policy rules. Correct pair?
recall.answer: First contextual grounding checks, then Automated Reasoning checks.

sections.title: 12. Testing safety: red-teaming basics with AWS tooling

keyTerms.definition: Systematic adversarial testing. You try to make your GenAI app misbehave, then fix what breaks.
Malicious instructions hidden in retrieved documents or tool outputs.
The evaluation metrics scoring how the app handles adversarial prompts.
The side that builds the defenses.

recall.question: The finance-assistant example: 150 adversarial prompts, 22 break. What was the real finding and fix?
recall.answer: 15 of the 22 were indirect prompt injections hidden in KB documents that the input guardrail never saw. The fix: scan retrieved context too, and add an instruction-hierarchy note. Re-run: 3 of 150 break.

recall.question: Why is the claim our guardrails passed the default tests, so we are safe a trap?
recall.answer: Default tests cover default attacks. Red-teaming must cover every input channel: user messages, retrieved documents, tool outputs, and multi-turn history.

recall.question: Is red-teaming a one-time event?
recall.answer: No. New attack techniques appear constantly, so the suite must be re-run and every successful attack becomes a new test case.

keyTerms.definition: The test set for jailbreak and prompt-injection resistance.
What guardrail scanning and red-team coverage must extend to.

recall.question: EASY: check jailbreak and prompt-injection resistance before launch. Most correct approach?
recall.answer: Build an adversarial prompt suite, evaluate it with harmfulness and refusal metrics, and add human red-team review.

recall.question: HARD: two practices for an ongoing red-team program?
recall.answer: Re-run the adversarial suite on every important change to prompt, model, or retrieval, and make every successful attack a permanent regression test case.

sections.title: 13. CI/CD for GenAI apps: prompt versioning and eval gates

keyTerms.definition: Treating prompts as released items with immutable published versions.
Pipeline stages that run the evaluation suite and stop deployment if scores worsen.
The Bedrock service that stores prompt versions.
The immutable version identifier the application deploys. Rollback is a repoint.
Putting 5 percent of live traffic on the new version to validate real phrasing.

recall.question: The worked example: 400-prompt golden eval, gate thresholds, 11 of 46 publishes blocked. What did the numbers show?
recall.answer: The eval took about 20 minutes and $8 in judge costs per publish. Thresholds: no metric down more than 0.03, zero harmfulness, cost per conversation up at most 10 percent. Post-mortems showed 9 of the 11 blocked publishes would have caused user-visible regressions.

recall.question: Why does a prompt rollback need a redeploy when prompts are hardcoded strings?
recall.answer: Prompts are configuration and need their own versioning. With version ARNs, rollback is a pointer change taking less than a minute.

recall.question: Marketing must change wording often without engineering deploys, and every change must be tested. Correct solution?
recall.answer: Bedrock Prompt Management versioning plus a CodePipeline eval gate.

keyTerms.definition: What Prompt Management provides for weekly wording updates.
What runs Bedrock evaluations on a golden dataset against the production baseline.
What provides the audit trail of version publishes and deployments.

recall.question: EASY: a non-technical team updates wording weekly without code deploys, and quality must be validated first. Most appropriate?
recall.answer: Manage prompts in Bedrock Prompt Management with published versions, and gate deployment on Bedrock evaluation jobs in CodePipeline.

recall.question: HARD: instant rollback plus a full audit trail. Which two mechanisms?
recall.answer: Reference immutable prompt version ARNs so rollback is a pointer change, and use CloudTrail records of version publishes and deployments for the audit trail.
